findings.source_passage: In turn, jerkingly raised and lowered by the rolling billows, the towing resistance of the log caused the old reelman to stagger strangely.
findings.why_it_matters: This vivid physical detail — the reelman staggering under the towing resistance — grounds the mechanical failure in embodied sensation and adds to the chapter's motif of instruments failing men; its loss flattens the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence about the reelman staggering before the 'Hold hard!' / snap sequence.

findings.source_passage: the skewer seems loosening out of the middle of the world. Haul in, haul in, Tahitian! These lines run whole, and whirling out: come in broken, and dragging slow. Ha, Pip? come to help; eh, Pip?
findings.why_it_matters: The Manxman's full speech — especially 'These lines run whole, and whirling out: come in broken, and dragging slow' — is a rhythmically distinctive, thematically loaded counterpoint to Ahab's boast; the draft cuts after 'middle of the world' and wrongly attributes the remainder to the Manxman as a generic mutter, erasing the cosmic resonance of the broken-line image.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full Manxman speech through 'Ha, Pip? come to help; eh, Pip?' before Pip's entrance, keeping the speaker attribution as in the source (Ishmael's narration, not the Manxman).

findings.source_passage: One daft with strength, the other daft with weakness. But here's the end of the rotten line—all dripping, too. Mend it, eh? I think we had best have a new line altogether. I'll see Mr. Stubb about it.
findings.why_it_matters: The Manxman's closing coda — 'One daft with strength, the other daft with weakness' plus the deflating practical joke about seeing Mr. Stubb — is the chapter's ironic signature close, balancing cosmic dread with mundane seamanship; the draft's truncated version loses both the thematic summary and the tonal descent.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full final Manxman speech, ending with 'I'll see Mr. Stubb about it,' to preserve the chapter's ironic close.

findings.source_passage: Where sayest thou Pip was, boy? / 'Astern there, sir, astern! Lo! lo!'
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The greater idiot ever scolds the lesser'
findings.why_it_matters: Ahab's question and Pip's excited directional cry are a small dramatic beat that the draft skips, jumping directly to Ahab's 'Who art thou, boy?' speech; the omission slightly compresses the recognition moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert Ahab's 'Where sayest thou Pip was, boy?' and Pip's 'Astern there, sir, astern! Lo! lo!' before the 'Who art thou' speech.

source_locator": "paragraph beginning 'What's this? here's velvet shark-skin'
findings.why_it_matters: Pip's tactile wonder at Ahab's hand ('velvet shark-skin') is the sensory prompt that motivates the man-rope speech; the draft begins with 'Ah, now, had poor Pip but felt so kind a thing as this' without establishing what the thing is, slightly disconnecting cause from effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Prepend 'What's this? here's velvet shark-skin,' intently gazing at Ahab's hand, and feeling it.' before Pip's man-rope speech.

summary: Three medium-severity losses — the staggering-reelman image, the Manxman's thematically loaded 'lines run whole … come in broken' speech, and the chapter's ironic final coda ('One daft with strength, the other daft with weakness … I'll see Mr. Stubb about it') — collectively deplete the chapter's voice and interpretive texture enough to require regeneration.
